subject: instability in N-mixture over-dispersed poisson model

messages.author: b3061e9ec8f1a7f2
messages.subject: instability in N-mixture over-dispersed poisson model
parts:
Hi All,

I have been using an overdispersed poisson N-mixture model of the type
found in section 12.3.3 of Bayesian Population Analysis Using
WinBUGS:A Hierarchical Perspective, to estimate green sturgeon from
sonar images. This model has worked well for data from previous years
and this years data set. However, I decided to do a more conservative
count from the images we collected this year as a sort of lower limit
to the estimate. The original count had ~4500 animals over 69 sites
with between 2 and 7 replicates for each site. The more selective
count had about ~3000. The counts per image can range from 0 to 230
so considerable variation. Unfortunately, the model for the more
conservative count went off the rails in a similar way that some
negative binomial N-mixture models do in that the detection
probability dropped from 0.6 to ~0.01 thus vastly increasing the
estimated abundance. Just looking at the two data sets, nothing
stands out to me as being crazy different. Just reducing the 4500
count data set by %50 does not cause the model to go off the rails. I
have narrowed the problem sites to those that have at least one 0 in
it and counts between 1-3 in the other replicates. If I change two
sites that have four 0's and a single 1 to five 1's, the model again
gives reasonable median abundance estimates though the upper 95% is
still relatively high and results vary between runs. But basically, I
add 8 animals (albeit strategically placed) to a survey of ~3000
animals and gain relative stability.

I find this to be concerning that the model is so sensitive. Anyone
have some wisdom to share?

I will attach the data and model in case anyone is curious to see it,
takes a couple minutes to run on my laptop. Run the entire script as
is to get the off the rails result. Follow the comment/uncomment
instructions on lines 237, 310 and 315 to run the model with +8
animals.

Thanks!
Brian

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: Re: instability in N-mixture over-dispersed poisson model
parts:
Dear Brian,

well, yes, estimates under the Nmix can sometimes be unstable. I agree that this is worrying, but on the other hand, at least the extreme case where abundance goes to infinity and detection to zero is simple to diagnose.

I would perhaps prefer a Bayesian solution with "weakly informative" priors to stabilize the estimates over your solution which appears more arbitrary.

Best regards  --- Marc

messages.subject: Re: instability in N-mixture over-dispersed poisson model
parts:
Hi Brian,

I have been browsing through your code. I have tried a model selection (null) with unmarked, and it selects the Negative Binomial (see below). The result of (state) backTransform on the first model is 25.4 SE: 7.76 and on the second 17.2 SE: 5.48, which is consistent with your selection. The detection hardly changes between the two models (0.482 SE: 0.00922 vs 0.458 SE: 0.0109). I imagine using the BUGS avenue should not give a very different result.
